newsitem.title: BELGIUM: German building industry sees no growth until 1998.
newsitem.headline: German building industry sees no growth until 1998.

text.p: The German building sector, which has suffered a long recession, will not see any growth until 1998, Otmar Franz, the president of the German building industry association, said on Wednesday.
The sector will show a decline in building volume of 3.3 percent for 1996, after a weak growth of 1.2 percent last year, Franz told journalists.
Franz said he expected another fall of 2.8 percent for 1997, before the sector finally recovers in 1998.

But Franz said the outlook was not so gloomy for the rest of Europe, forecasting a decline in 1996 of one percent and then weak growth of 0.2 percent for 1997, although he said the European industry would be strongly affected by Germany.
Despite the current decline, Franz said he saw excellent prospects for the medium and long term in Europe.
Franz said the European Union should structurally reform its budget and dedicate funds currently going to farming to transport, telecommunications and environmental protection.
